tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

    name: 'review-changes',

    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,

    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>

    ))

# 2026-09-30: Mike's refresh fix

## What and why
Coach Mike Wenger could not refresh the volleyball workbook (Power Query merges Kinexon
exports from `Box\Kinexon\Kinexon Raw Data`). Goal: he refreshes on his own, Eric not involved.

## Root cause
Box Drive opens the workbook in Excel as `https://api.box.com/wopi/files/...`, so the old
Ref!D2 (`ExportPath`) formula, which searched `CELL("filename")` for `\Box\`, was blank for
everyone. Refresh only worked via the hardcoded `C:\Users\eric_rash\...` fallback; Mike's
fallback was a guessed `michael_wenger` username.

## Decisions
- D2 takes `C:\Users\<name>\` from the file path when local, else `INFO("directory")`, plus
  `Box\Kinexon\Kinexon Raw Data`. Kept the hardcoded paths as fallbacks.
- Rejected: scanning `C:\Users` in Power Query. Access-denied profiles (here
  `CodexSandboxOffline`) raise a credentials error `try` cannot catch.
- Rejected: a separate shared "Raw Data Files" query; cross-query references tripped the
  privacy firewall on this machine.
- A folder counts only if one export's Overview tab reads; Sample File takes the first readable
  export; friendly Error.Record if nothing works (Codex review points).
- Workbook set to ignore privacy levels (FastCombine); all sources are local folders.
- Codex review ran on gpt-5.6-sol because gpt-6.1-sol needs API-key login; Eric kept 5.6.

## Files
- `workbooks/VB_Revised_refresh-fix.xlsx`: the fixed workbook (5,581,455 bytes).
- `scripts/fix_refresh_path.ps1`: rebuilds it from a copy of the Box file; `-SimulateMike` and
  `-D2Override` are test modes that never save.
- `docs/context.md`, `docs/STATUS.md`, `docs/mike-refresh-checklist.md`, this file.

## Tests (Eric's laptop, copies only)
D2 only with both usernames broken: 7,069 rows. D2 at an empty folder: fallback wins.
Junk first file: skipped (245 rows from 2 real files). Everything broken: fails.
Not tested on Mike's laptop.

## Mid-flight
- Eric uploaded the fix and renamed it `VB_Revised_.xlsx`. The local Box copy was blocked by a
  hidden Excel (closed) then Box Drive was force-restarted and now `streem.exe` crashes on
  launch. Needs a Windows restart. Content of the Box file not yet confirmed.
- Branch `fix/mike-refresh-path` not merged to main.

## Next
See `docs/STATUS.md` > Next.

**What we fixed**
- **The problem:** Mike couldn't refresh the workbook. Box Drive opens the file in Excel as a web link, not as a `C:\` file path. Because of that, the cell that tells Power Query where to find the raw Kinexon data folder (Ref!D2) was always blank, for everyone. It only worked for you because there was a backup path hardcoded to your username.
- **The fix:** D2 now builds the path from whoever has the file open, `C:\Users\<name>\Box\Kinexon\Kinexon Raw Data`. If no export in a folder can be read, the workbook skips that folder. If nothing works at all, it shows a clear error. Privacy levels are set to ignore, since every source is a local folder.
- **Testing:** It passed on your laptop using copies, including a run that pretended to be Mike. It has **not** been tested on Mike's laptop.

- `Box\Kinexon\SandBox\VB_Revised_.xlsx` is in your Box folder, but it shows no size. That usually means Box hasn't downloaded it to the laptop yet. So I still can't confirm it's the fixed version, which should be 5,581,455 bytes and show a `C:\Users\...` path in Ref!D2.

**Next steps**
1. Open `VB_Revised_.xlsx` from Box. That makes Box download it. Then I'll check the size and Ref!D2.

content.text:
I found the cause, and it's fixable.

**What happened:** The query code in the Box file is identical to our 9/30 fix. What changed is the workbook's "Ignore privacy levels" setting: it's switched back off in the Box file, though our fixed copy has it on. That setting was the only thing keeping this error from happening, so it's back. It most likely got reset when the file was saved at 9:08 or renamed at 9:10 (`VB_Revised_.xlsx` became `VB_Revised.xlsx`).

**To get yourself working right now (about 30 seconds):**
In Excel, go to Data → Get Data → Query Options → **Current Workbook → Privacy** → choose **"Ignore the Privacy Levels"**, click OK, then save and Refresh All. While you have that window open, also look at **Global → Privacy**. If it says "Always combine data according to your Privacy Level settings for each source," that overrides the per-workbook switch, so tell me what it says.

**That's only a band-aid.** If something can switch that setting off once, it can do it again, and Mike's own Excel settings can override it on his laptop. The real fix is to merge the five Power Query queries into one. The error comes from one query using results from another query while also reading a data source. With a single query, that can't happen. I'll test it on a copy with the privacy check switched **on**, so it proves the fix works without the band-aid. I won't touch the live Box file, and Mike doesn't get the checklist until that test passes.

Two quick questions before I build it:
1. **How did you open the file this morning?** From the Box folder in File Explorer, or from the Box website ("Open in Excel" / Excel Online)? Mike will open it the same way, and the web route may be what reset the setting.
2. **Did you rename it to `VB_Revised.xlsx` (no underscore)?** The docs and Mike's checklist still use the underscore name, so I'll update them to match.

param([string]$Src,[string]$Out,[switch]$SimulateMike,[string]$D2Override='')
# Builds the refresh-fixed workbook from a copy of VB_Revised.xlsx.
# Test switches (the file is never saved when either is used):
#   -SimulateMike   breaks both hardcoded username paths, so refresh must succeed through Ref!D2 alone.
#   -D2Override     types a literal path into Ref!D2 (e.g. an empty folder, to check the fallbacks kick in).
$ErrorActionPreference='Stop'
Copy-Item $Src $Out -Force

# User profile root (C:\Users\<name>\) from the file's own path when it is local,
# else from INFO("directory") (the user's Documents folder), because Box Drive opens
# the file as an https://api.box.com/wopi/... link and CELL("filename") has no local path.
$p  = 'IF(UPPER(LEFT(CELL("filename",A1),9))="C:\USERS\",CELL("filename",A1),INFO("directory"))'
$d2 = '=IFERROR(LEFT(' + $p + ',FIND("\",' + $p + ',10))&"Box\Kinexon\Kinexon Raw Data","")'

param([string]$Src,[string]$Out,[switch]$FirewallOn,[switch]$Baseline,[switch]$SimulateMike)
# Makes Kinexon Master a single self-contained query so refresh no longer depends on the
# workbook's "Ignore privacy levels" switch (Box/Excel reset it on 2026-10-02 and refresh failed
# with "references other queries or steps ... Please rebuild this data combination").
# Run on a copy of the current Box file (after fix_refresh_path.ps1 has been applied).
# Test switches (the file is never saved when any is used):
#   -FirewallOn    turns "Ignore privacy levels" OFF, so the privacy firewall is active.
#   -Baseline      skips the rewrite (with -FirewallOn this should reproduce the error).
#   -SimulateMike  breaks both hardcoded username paths, so refresh must succeed through Ref!D2 alone.
$ErrorActionPreference='Stop'
Copy-Item $Src $Out -Force

$transform = @'
    // Reads one Kinexon export's Overview tab. Kept inside this query on purpose: referencing another
    // query here trips the Power Query privacy firewall ("Please rebuild this data combination").
    TransformFile = (bin as binary) => Table.PromoteHeaders(
        Excel.Workbook(bin, null, true){[Item="Overview",Kind="Sheet"]}[Data], [PromoteAllScalars=true]),
    // A file counts only if its Overview tab actually reads.
    IsGood = (bin) => (try TransformFile(bin) otherwise null) <> null,
'@
$helpers = 'Transform Sample File','Parameter1','Sample File','Transform File'

$xl = New-Object -ComObject Excel.Application; $xl.Visible=$false; $xl.DisplayAlerts=$false
try {
  $wb = $xl.Workbooks.Open($Out)
  if (-not $Baseline) {
    $q = $wb.Queries.Item('Kinexon Master'); $f = $q.Formula
    $f2 = [regex]::Replace($f, '    // A file counts only if its Overview tab actually reads\.\r?\n    IsGood = \(bin\) => \(try #"Transform File"\(bin\) otherwise null\) <> null,\r?\n', $transform.Replace('$','$$') + "`r`n")
    $f2 = $f2.Replace('try #"Transform File"([Content])', 'try TransformFile([Content])')
    $f2 = $f2.Replace('Table.ColumnNames(#"Transform File"(#"Sample File"))', 'Table.ColumnNames(TransformFile(Table.First(Table.SelectRows(Source, each IsGood([Content])))[Content]))')
    foreach ($h in $helpers) { if ($f2.Contains('#"' + $h + '"') -or $f2 -match "\b$h\b(?!\s*=)" -and $h -eq 'Parameter1') { throw "Kinexon Master still references $h" } }
    if (-not $f2.Contains('TransformFile = ')) { throw 'IsGood step did not match' }
    if ($SimulateMike) { $f2 = $f2.Replace('eric_rash\Box','nobody_x\Box').Replace('michael_wenger','nobody_y') }
    $q.Formula = $f2
    foreach ($h in $helpers) { $wb.Queries.Item($h).Delete() }
    "queries now: " + (($wb.Queries | ForEach-Object { $_.Name }) -join ', ')
  }
  $wb.Queries.FastCombine = -not $FirewallOn
  $xl.CalculateFull()
  "D2 now: " + $wb.Worksheets.Item('Ref').Range('D2').Text

  $lo = $wb.Worksheets.Item('Kinexon Master').ListObjects.Item(1)
  $before = $lo.ListRows.Count
  $lo.ListRows.Item(1).Range.Cells.Item(1,1).Value2 = 'SENTINEL'
  $c = $lo.QueryTable.WorkbookConnection; $c.OLEDBConnection.BackgroundQuery = $false
  $ok = $true; try { $c.Refresh() } catch { $ok = $false; "REFRESH FAILED: " + $_.Exception.Message }
  $first = $lo.ListRows.Item(1).Range.Cells.Item(1,1).Text
  "rows before=$before after=" + $lo.ListRows.Count + " firstcell=$first"
  "FastCombine=" + $wb.Queries.FastCombine
  if ($ok -and $first -ne 'SENTINEL' -and -not ($FirewallOn -or $Baseline -or $SimulateMike)) { $c.OLEDBConnection.BackgroundQuery = $true; $wb.Save(); "SAVED $Out" } else { "NOT SAVED" }
  $wb.Close($false)
} finally { $xl.Quit() }

# Volleyball GRID — transferred workbook context

Carried over Sept 2026. Read before editing or troubleshooting the workbook.

## Where the canonical file lives

Canonical copy is `VB_Revised_.xlsx` in `Box\Kinexon\SandBox` (renamed 2026-09-30 when
the refresh fix was uploaded; earlier names: VB_Revised, Volleyball_Revised, Volleyball_GROUP). A working copy sits at
`OneDrive > 00_Primary_Storage_Drive > 02_SPORTS > Volleyball > SandBox`.

Two versions had diverged (Volleyball_GRID vs Volleyball_v2) and were merged into a
single GRID file in Aug 2026.

## Refresh workflow

Drop the source export into the Box source folder, then Refresh All on the dashboard.
Everything else updates from there.

Power Query pulls from `Box\Kinexon\Kinexon Raw Data` (the old "Session Exports 8.13"
folder is now in `Box\Kinexon\ARCHIVE`). Only the Overview tab of each session file
merges into the master dataset, via the `Kinexon_Master` table.

Shared with Michael Wenger, who refreshes it on his own machine. Step-by-step for him:
`docs/mike-refresh-checklist.md`.

### How the query finds the folder (fixed 2026-09-30)

Ref!D2 (defined name `ExportPath`) builds `C:\Users\<signed-in user>\Box\Kinexon\Kinexon Raw Data`,
and both `Kinexon Master` and `Sample File` read that first.

**Why it broke for Mike:** Box Drive opens the workbook in Excel as a web link
(`https://api.box.com/wopi/files/...`), not a `C:\` path. The old D2 formula searched
`CELL("filename")` for `\Box\`, found nothing, and was blank for everyone. Refresh only
worked through the hardcoded fallbacks, and Mike's fallback was a guessed username
(`michael_wenger`).

**The fix:** D2 now takes `C:\Users\<name>\` from the file path when it is local, else
from `INFO("directory")` (the signed-in user's Documents folder), then appends
`Box\Kinexon\Kinexon Raw Data`. The two hardcoded paths stay as fallbacks. A path only
counts if at least one export in it actually reads (Overview tab loads), so an empty or
half-synced folder falls through to the next path. If none work, the query stops with a
plain message telling the user to check Box Drive or type the folder path into Ref!D2.
`Sample File` takes the first export that reads, so one bad file cannot break the column
list. The workbook's privacy setting is "ignore privacy levels" (all sources are local
folders), so no privacy prompt appears on a new machine.

Known limit: if a user's Documents folder is redirected off `C:\Users` (e.g. `D:\`), D2
comes out wrong; typing the folder path into D2 fixes it.

Verified 2026-09-30 on Eric's machine (copies, not the live file): D2 only with both

# Volleyball GRID — transferred workbook context

Carried over Sept 2026. Read before editing or troubleshooting the workbook.

## Where the canonical file lives

Canonical copy is `VB_Revised_.xlsx` in `Box\Kinexon\SandBox` (renamed 2026-09-30 when
the refresh fix was uploaded; earlier names: VB_Revised, Volleyball_Revised, Volleyball_GROUP). A working copy sits at
`OneDrive > 00_Primary_Storage_Drive > 02_SPORTS > Volleyball > SandBox`.

Two versions had diverged (Volleyball_GRID vs Volleyball_v2) and were merged into a
single GRID file in Aug 2026.

## Refresh workflow

Drop the source export into the Box source folder, then Refresh All on the dashboard.
Everything else updates from there.

folder is now in `Box\Kinexon\ARCHIVE`). Only the Overview tab of each session file
merges into the master dataset, via the `Kinexon_Master` table.

Shared with Michael Wenger, who refreshes it on his own machine. Step-by-step for him:
`docs/mike-refresh-checklist.md`.

### How the query finds the folder (fixed 2026-09-30)

Ref!D2 (defined name `ExportPath`) builds `C:\Users\<signed-in user>\Box\Kinexon\Kinexon Raw Data`,
and `Kinexon Master` reads that first. Since 2026-10-02 it is the workbook's only query (see below).

**Why it broke for Mike:** Box Drive opens the workbook in Excel as a web link
(`https://api.box.com/wopi/files/...`), not a `C:\` path. The old D2 formula searched
`CELL("filename")` for `\Box\`, found nothing, and was blank for everyone. Refresh only
worked through the hardcoded fallbacks, and Mike's fallback was a guessed username
(`michael_wenger`).

**The fix:** D2 now takes `C:\Users\<name>\` from the file path when it is local, else
from `INFO("directory")` (the signed-in user's Documents folder), then appends
`Box\Kinexon\Kinexon Raw Data`. The two hardcoded paths stay as fallbacks. A path only
counts if at least one export in it actually reads (Overview tab loads), so an empty or
half-synced folder falls through to the next path. If none work, the query stops with a
plain message telling the user to check Box Drive or type the folder path into Ref!D2.
`Sample File` takes the first export that reads, so one bad file cannot break the column
list. The workbook's privacy setting is "ignore privacy levels" (all sources are local
folders), so no privacy prompt appears on a new machine.

Known limit: if a user's Documents folder is redirected off `C:\Users` (e.g. `D:\`), D2
comes out wrong; typing the folder path into D2 fixes it.

Verified 2026-09-30 on Eric's machine (copies, not the live file): D2 only with both
usernames broken, D2 pointing at an empty folder, a junk first file, and everything
broken (fails, as it should). Codex (gpt-5.6-sol) reviewed the M and D2 logic; its two
hardening points are in. Besides the intended changes, Excel's save rewrites some
internal bookkeeping (style count 628 to 626, pivot cache id); no visible formatting change.

Rebuild script: `scripts/fix_refresh_path.ps1`.

**Do not** make the query scan `C:\Users` for the folder. Tried 2026-09-30: an
access-denied profile folder (another account on the laptop) raises a credentials error
that `try` cannot catch, and the refresh fails.

## Two operational traps

**A workbook open in Excel makes automated saves silently no-op.** Excel serves a
read-only copy. Close it before applying changes.

**Box overrules local file operations on the sync folder.** Renames and deletes get
reverted; rapid repeated writes produce conflict copies and a read-only flag. Work on a
copy outside Box, then upload one new version of the existing file through Box on the web.

## Thresholds

Load thresholds (team, position, individual) are frozen to the Practices 1-18 baseline,
the last practice before the first regular-season match (18 Aug 2026, Honolulu), so
light/medium/hard classifications do not drift as the season adds data. Live percentile
formulas sit parked on Load Thresholds L11:Q45, unapplied.

Matches are deliberately excluded from load thresholds. Revisit once regular-season
matches accumulate.

Note: Kinexon changed the jump-height bands from absolute feet to % of max between
export versions.

## Capacity and layout

- Roster is 16 athletes. The Athlete Load Grid was opened to 24 slots (grid rows 7-30,
  GD-1 block rows 35-58) so new athletes calculate automatically.
- Process Behavior session index raised 100 to 300 sessions, matching Load Monitoring
  rows 51-350. Practice XmR raised 100 to 200.
- An athlete with no frozen individual threshold now falls back to her position band
  instead of returning #N/A.
- Charts are driven by `cs_*` defined names (OFFSET spans off helper cells Ref!B25:B29)

  two most recent matches with session data via Ref!B21:B24.
- Drill cost map rebuilt as 124 series covering Drill Library rows 8-127, labels and
  values from live helper columns T/U, colored by quadrant, so new drills appear
  automatically.
- Periodization calendar rows 40+ used to need the session ID typed into column E by
  hand. C/D/E now auto-fill from Load Monitoring by date; a date with more sessions than
  calendar rows shows a "(+N more this day)" flag on its last row.

The Game XmR block on Process Behavior still summarises only its first 100 rows.

# Volleyball GRID — transferred workbook context

Carried over Sept 2026. Read before editing or troubleshooting the workbook.

## Where the canonical file lives

Canonical copy is `VB_Revised.xlsx` in `Box\Kinexon\SandBox` (Eric renamed it back on
2026-10-02; it was `VB_Revised_.xlsx` 9/30–10/2; earlier names: Volleyball_Revised, Volleyball_GROUP). A working copy sits at
`OneDrive > 00_Primary_Storage_Drive > 02_SPORTS > Volleyball > SandBox`.

Two versions had diverged (Volleyball_GRID vs Volleyball_v2) and were merged into a
single GRID file in Aug 2026.

## Refresh workflow

Drop the source export into the Box source folder, then Refresh All on the dashboard.
Everything else updates from there.

Power Query pulls from `Box\Kinexon\Kinexon Raw Data` (the old "Session Exports 8.13"
folder is now in `Box\Kinexon\ARCHIVE`). Only the Overview tab of each session file
merges into the master dataset, via the `Kinexon_Master` table.

Shared with Michael Wenger, who refreshes it on his own machine. Step-by-step for him:
`docs/mike-refresh-checklist.md`.

### How the query finds the folder (fixed 2026-09-30)

Ref!D2 (defined name `ExportPath`) builds `C:\Users\<signed-in user>\Box\Kinexon\Kinexon Raw Data`,
and `Kinexon Master` reads that first. Since 2026-10-02 it is the workbook's only query (see below).

**Why it broke for Mike:** Box Drive opens the workbook in Excel as a web link
(`https://api.box.com/wopi/files/...`), not a `C:\` path. The old D2 formula searched
`CELL("filename")` for `\Box\`, found nothing, and was blank for everyone. Refresh only
worked through the hardcoded fallbacks, and Mike's fallback was a guessed username
(`michael_wenger`).

**The fix:** D2 now takes `C:\Users\<name>\` from the file path when it is local, else
from `INFO("directory")` (the signed-in user's Documents folder), then appends
`Box\Kinexon\Kinexon Raw Data`. The two hardcoded paths stay as fallbacks. A path only
counts if at least one export in it actually reads (Overview tab loads), so an empty or
half-synced folder falls through to the next path. If none work, the query stops with a
plain message telling the user to check Box Drive or type the folder path into Ref!D2.
`Sample File` takes the first export that reads, so one bad file cannot break the column
list. The workbook's privacy setting is "ignore privacy levels" (all sources are local
folders), so no privacy prompt appears on a new machine.

Known limit: if a user's Documents folder is redirected off `C:\Users` (e.g. `D:\`), D2
comes out wrong; typing the folder path into D2 fixes it.

Verified 2026-09-30 on Eric's machine (copies, not the live file): D2 only with both
usernames broken, D2 pointing at an empty folder, a junk first file, and everything
broken (fails, as it should). Codex (gpt-5.6-sol) reviewed the M and D2 logic; its two
hardening points are in. Besides the intended changes, Excel's save rewrites some
internal bookkeeping (style count 628 to 626, pivot cache id); no visible formatting change.

Rebuild script: `scripts/fix_refresh_path.ps1`.

**Do not** make the query scan `C:\Users` for the folder. Tried 2026-09-30: an
access-denied profile folder (another account on the laptop) raises a credentials error
that `try` cannot catch, and the refresh fails.

## Two operational traps

**A workbook open in Excel makes automated saves silently no-op.** Excel serves a
read-only copy. Close it before applying changes.

**Box overrules local file operations on the sync folder.** Renames and deletes get
reverted; rapid repeated writes produce conflict copies and a read-only flag. Work on a
copy outside Box, then upload one new version of the existing file through Box on the web.

## Thresholds

Load thresholds (team, position, individual) are frozen to the Practices 1-18 baseline,
the last practice before the first regular-season match (18 Aug 2026, Honolulu), so
light/medium/hard classifications do not drift as the season adds data. Live percentile
formulas sit parked on Load Thresholds L11:Q45, unapplied.

Matches are deliberately excluded from load thresholds. Revisit once regular-season
matches accumulate.

Note: Kinexon changed the jump-height bands from absolute feet to % of max between
export versions.

## Capacity and layout

- Roster is 16 athletes. The Athlete Load Grid was opened to 24 slots (grid rows 7-30,
  GD-1 block rows 35-58) so new athletes calculate automatically.
- Process Behavior session index raised 100 to 300 sessions, matching Load Monitoring
  rows 51-350. Practice XmR raised 100 to 200.
- An athlete with no frozen individual threshold now falls back to her position band
  instead of returning #N/A.
- Charts are driven by `cs_*` defined names (OFFSET spans off helper cells Ref!B25:B29)
  so each chart sizes to the data instead of plotting empty rows. GD Profile follows the
  two most recent matches with session data via Ref!B21:B24.
- Drill cost map rebuilt as 124 series covering Drill Library rows 8-127, labels and
  values from live helper columns T/U, colored by quadrant, so new drills appear
  automatically.
- Periodization calendar rows 40+ used to need the session ID typed into column E by
  hand. C/D/E now auto-fill from Load Monitoring by date; a date with more sessions than
  calendar rows shows a "(+N more this day)" flag on its last row.

## Known open issue

The Game XmR block on Process Behavior still summarises only its first 100 rows.

## Related

- Kinexon_Volleyball, Football_GRID (which ports design from here), volleyball data hub

- "Ignore privacy levels" is still switched on in the new file as a backup, but refresh no longer depends on it.
